AfterCardExhausted.maps_to: on_card_exhausted (forgotten_soul.py:25-39), dispatched by HookSystem.on_card_exhausted (hooks.py:415-418) from ExhaustCmd (cmds.py:371)
AfterCardExhausted.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. Every number and stream matches -- DamageVar(1m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (ForgottenSoul.cs:16) is DAMAGE = 1 with DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED (= ValueProp.UNPOWERED, valueprops.py:42), the dealer is the player's own creature on both sides, and Rng.CombatTargets is combat.combat_rng.targets. The single divergence is the target SET: C# picks from `CombatState.HittableEnemies`, the sim from Relic.living_enemies() (G1, dormant).

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): `CombatState.HittableEnemies` (ForgottenSoul.cs:23) vs the sim's living_enemies() (forgotten_soul.py:28, relics/base.py:294-297)
guards.issue: Same mechanism, same verdict as audit/records/relic/bag_of_marbles.json guard G2 -- binding rule 3, so this entry cites rather than re-derives. C# targets `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(...)`; Relic.living_enemies() filters on `not e.is_gone` only, so an alive-but-unhittable enemy can be picked by the sim and is skipped by C#. Distinct from bag_of_marbles' instance in ONE way worth recording: Forgotten Soul fires on any exhaust, at any point in the combat, so bag_of_marbles' 'turn 1 only' dormancy argument does NOT carry over -- the only ported should_allow_hitting implementer, IllusionPower's is_reviving window (powers.py:1572-1575), is reachable on later turns. What keeps it dormant here is narrower: the pick happens through combat_rng.targets.choice(living), so an unhittable-but-alive enemy is merely eligible to be CHOSEN, and DamageCmd then applies the should_allow_hitting predicate itself (relics/base.py:296's own docstring) -- the observable is that the 1 damage lands on nobody instead of on a hittable enemy, which needs an exhaust to happen while a reviving Illusion enemy is in the combat alongside another live enemy. Porting any longer-lived untargetable state, or a second should_allow_hitting implementer, makes it live.

guards.what: N1: `card.Owner == base.Owner` (ForgottenSoul.cs:20); the sim checks no owner
guards.rationale: Multiplayer-only -- it stops one player's relic reacting to another player's exhaust. The sim's CombatState holds exactly one player and every card in the combat belongs to it (combat.py:112-116, 122-128). Waived under the shared contract's multiplayer exclusion.

guards.what: N2: the sim ADDS `if self.combat is None or self.combat.is_over: return` (forgotten_soul.py:26-27), which C# does not write here
guards.rationale: C# gates this centrally instead: Hook dispatchers bail on CombatManager.Instance.IsOverOrEnding, which audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json step 46 records the sim as having no counterpart for -- so a per-relic guard is how the sim reproduces it. The `self.combat is None` half covers a relic sitting on RunState.relics with no combat attached, which C# cannot reach because RelicModel only receives combat hooks from a live CombatState. Same observable either way.

guards.what: N3: ValueProp.Unpowered -- Strength must not scale the 1 damage
guards.rationale: Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): exhausting a Defend takes the enemy 56 -> 55 both with no Strength and with Strength 5. DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED is exactly ValueProp.UNPOWERED (valueprops.py:42), matching the DamageVar's prop, and the dealer is still passed (dealer=self.player) so damage-dealt hooks that do not read Strength still see the player as the source, as in C# (`base.Owner.Creature`).

guards.what: N4: `self._check_win()` after the damage (forgotten_soul.py:39); C# has no explicit call
guards.rationale: CreatureCmd.Damage runs the game's own death/win checking, and the sim's DamageCmd does not close a combat that a relic's out-of-band damage decides -- Relic._check_win (relics/base.py:299-304) exists for exactly that and its docstring says so. The observable is the same: exhausting the last card that kills the last enemy ends the combat on both sides.
